summary: Recent advancements in AI highlight significant developments and funding news. Google DeepMind launched Gemini 3.8 Live, introducing a Live Avatar to enhance user interaction. OpenAI's Proaction reported a 60% sales increase and substantial time savings by leveraging Codex for fleet management solutions. Hugging Face unveiled LFM2.5-VL-DSpark, a method to improve vision-language model efficiency, while Microsoft Research demonstrated that offloading AI inference can enhance robot performance in real-world tasks. Additionally, the AI startup TrustedRouter secured $1.25 million in funding, underscoring the growing investment in innovative AI solutions.

items.rewritten: Hugging Face has introduced a new method called LFM2.5-VL-DSpark to enhance the performance of vision-language models. This approach aims to accelerate the processing capabilities of these models, making them more efficient and effective.

items.original: Offloaded inference for real-world physical AI robotics. Robots are getting smarter, but how can their hardware match that growth? New Microsoft Research findings show that moving AI inference beyond the robot can improve task success, boost efficiency, and support more advanced physical AI workloads. The post Offloaded inference for real-world physical AI robotics appeared first on Microsoft Research .
items.rewritten: Microsoft Research has found that offloading AI inference from robots can significantly improve their performance in real-world tasks. This research suggests that by processing AI tasks externally, robots can become more efficient and capable of handling complex physical workloads.
